what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/decide-with-a-method: decisions a person's AI makes with a method, kept as the person's own decision records.

payload.label: Bring back my similar decisions
payload.job: When I am about to decide something, show what I decided in similar decisions before, what came next and how each turned out
payload.description: Reads the person's own decision records. The newest ones are weighed by the words their goals share with the named decision's goal, plus a point for the same method (read-data/decide-with-a-method.json `similar`). The closest are kept, closest first, limit of them (10 when not given, never more than 50). Each comes back with its goal, its method, the option it chose, its next action, its status (from its own current evidence) and its observed and reported results. Only those few are read whole, and nothing leaves the person's account.

decision_id.description: The decision about to be made

payload.label: Start a decision with my method
payload.job: Start a decision my AI will make with my method: what is being decided, the facts and constraints, and the options only if I already hold them
payload.description: Opens a decision in the person's own records from a source_id (the same source always opens the same decision; the same input again is that decision, different input is refused), its goal, its evidence ({ref, claim}, each ref unique: the facts and every non-negotiable constraint) and the options ({id, label}, at least two). The decision is answered by the rows of one method, a saved view over the person's method rows (the one named, else their default view): read it with tool:read-a-method and record answers to any number of its rows in one call with tool:record-method-answers. Returns case_id.

source_id.description: Unique text naming where this decision comes from

method.description: The saved view over the person's method rows this decision is answered by (their default method view when left out)

parent_decision_id.description: A decision of the person's this one is a child of (never itself)

payload.job: Close decisions that will never be carried on, and keep why
payload.description: Sets each named decision's status to ended and keeps the status it had (previous_status), ended_at, ended_by and ended_because, with every other field unchanged and nothing deleted. Each write is conditioned on the value just read: a decision that changed meanwhile answers conflict. A decision whose root is too large to send with its condition in one 64 KiB message is ended through its record layout instead, checked by a second read just before the write, and answers laid_apart. One the door still refuses as too large is left as it was and answers too_large. A decision in outcome_verified, correction_needed or verification is not ended. 1 to 256 decisions per call.

payload.label: See my decisions
payload.job: Show my decisions, what I am working toward, my plans and what has helped me decide
payload.description: Reads your own rows and answers the Decisions screen: your newest decisions (at most 100) as summaries with the pursuits each cites, where each stands and how far it has got (decided, next action carried out, result checked); your current pursuits as the tree they nest into (from your record-scope choice rows); your newest plans; and what has helped you (which questions changed your answers and how those decisions turned out). With native_collection_page it answers one bounded page instead: the facts what helped is counted from (helped_items, your method check questions and your AIs' recorded work), collection_coverage saying whether more decisions, pursuits or plans exist, and next_before to send as before for the next page. access and allowance are what your computer reports: when your access limits deciding and does not keep decisions, the answer is free with nothing listed; none reported is no limit. metadata_only answers only access, allowance and the words for no pursuits, and reads no row. It changes nothing.

metadata_only.description: Answer only access, allowance and the no-pursuits words; read no row

native_collection_page.description: One bounded page with its coverage, instead of the whole what-helped view

before.description: The next_before an earlier page answered: the page starts below this created_at

access.description: What your computer reports: { capabilities: [names], limits?: { [access]: [{ count, per }] } }

allowance.description: What your computer reports of your decision allowance: { count, per, used }

space_pursuits.description: The pursuits your spaces share, shown beside your own

payload.label: Answer the Decisions page
payload.job: Answer the Trillion page route GET /work/api/decisions: the Decisions screen's rows, as old Trillion answered them
payload.description: A page route tool: the engine runs it for the page's account with { path, method, query, body, browser } and answers the page with { status, body }. GET /decisions answers 200 with the Decisions screen's rows, the same read as tool:see-my-decisions with no input: { free, summaries, pursuits, space_pursuits, plans, access, allowance, pursuits_words, helped }. Any other path or method answers 404 { error: "Not found" }. It changes nothing.

payload.label: Answer the page's pursuits
payload.job: List what I am pursuing now, and keep a goal I add or change from the page
payload.description: The page route /pursuits: GET answers { pursuits } (every pursuit that is not ended or archived); PUT { pursuits: [{ title, now, after, ... }], replace_all? } adds or updates each pursuit by its id (made from its id or title), and with replace_all ends every current pursuit left out except one with a room, then answers every current pursuit. Each pursuit is one pursuit record. A pursuit missing its title, now or after is refused 400 with { error }, as old trillion's DecisionEngine refused it; any other route answers 404.

query.description: The route's query parameters, by name

body.description: The JSON body the page sent ({} when none)

browser.description: The asking browser's own facts: user_agent, origin, visitor

payload.label: Record a decision I made myself
payload.job: When I have already decided, keep my own verdict as the decision, with my exact words and when I said them, without my AI walking the method's questions
payload.description: The person decided; this keeps their verdict as the decision. Only the person's own word is taken: person.message_id names the message row they sent (type message, speaker person) and person.said must be their exact words in it, or the run comes from their own signed-in page, which the engine attests as the task's origin and no input can set. An AI saying the person decided, with neither, is refused and told to answer the rows of the method (tool:read-a-method, tool:record-method-answers, then tool:make-the-decision), which every decision an AI makes still needs. The person's words are kept as an evidence row (person-verdict-<generation>) with where and when they said them; the decision and its root say decided_by person and method_walked false. A decision already made moves to decision_history. next_action and success_measure are what the AI will do now and how it will know it worked. The same verdict again replays.

decision_id.description: The decision the person decided (from tool:start-a-decision)

option_id.description: The option the person chose, one of the decision's options

next_action.description: What you will do now to carry out the person's decision

success_measure.description: How you will both know it worked

person.description: Where the person said it: message_id names the message row they sent, and said is their exact words in it. From their own signed-in page, said alone (the page's run is the source).

said.description: The person's exact words, as they wrote them

message_id.description: The message row the person sent (type message, speaker person)

payload.label: Read one of my methods
payload.job: Read the rows of one of my methods, a saved view over my method rows, a page at a time, each row with how strictly an answer to it is checked
payload.description: A method is a saved view over the person's method rows (their files and the sections of their files, each row whole): the view's rules keep the rows, its sort orders them, and any mix of rows is a method. Reads the saved view `method` (the id of a record of type list-view) and answers a page of its rows in the view's order, each with its whole values and the strictness an answer to it is checked by (its own `strictness` value, else the method's, else the default cheap check), and `next` to pass as `after` for the following page, null on the last. A page holds at most `limit` rows (25 when not given) and at most the bytes read-data/method-rows.json allows. Reads only; it writes nothing. The rows are those of the list the view is over, read by the list reader's own rule filter, so the method means what the person's own view of the list shows. Answer what you read with tool:record-method-answers.

method.description: The id of the saved view that is the method

after.description: The next of the page before, to read on

limit.description: How many rows at most in this page

payload.label: Record my answers to a method
payload.job: Record my AI's answers to any number of the rows of a method in one call, each with the rows it cites and the decision's evidence it rests on
payload.description: Records answers to a method's rows for a decision: input { decision_id, method, answers: [{ row, answer, cites?, evidence_refs? }], by? }, any number of answers, each about one row of the method (tool:read-a-method). An answer is recorded only when its row is a row of the method, every row it cites is a row of the method, every evidence ref it cites is evidence of the decision (or one of the person's current pursuits), and it passes its strictness: an open value on the row, else on the method, else the default (the answer says something and cites a row or a piece of evidence), a rule tree in the vocabulary of the person's view rules. A review by an AI is asked only where the strictness says review: that answer is kept with review asked. Nothing asks a judge. An answer that fails is named with why and nothing of it is written; the others are recorded, so one wrong answer never holds up the rest. The same answer again is unchanged; a different one is the row's next version. Answers are records of their own, one per decision and row. Returns recorded, unchanged, refused, how many rows of the method the decision has answered and how many the method has.

decision_id.description: The decision these answers are for

method.description: The id of the saved view that is the method

by.description: Who answered; the calling AI when not given

row.description: The id of a row of the method, as tool:read-a-method gave it

cites.description: Ids of rows of the method the answer rests on

evidence_refs.description: Refs of the decision's evidence the answer rests on

answers.answer: A made-up answer that rests on the made-up evidence
